) Data Preparation:
a) Download the Sample RNA-seq Count Matrix and associated Metadata.
```{r}
# Load libraries
library(tidyverse)

# Read in the data
setwd("/Users/juliannemirmina/Downloads/711_Course/Final Project")
counts <- read.csv("counts.csv", row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE)
meta   <- read.csv("meta_data.csv")

#The Cancer Genome Atlas Network. (2012). Comprehensive molecular portraits of human breast tumours. *Nature*, *490*(7418), 61-70. https://doi.org/10.1038/nature11412

```

2) Gene Selection and Summary Statistics:
a) Select One Gene: choose a gene from the dataset that interests you.
```{r}
# Pull out the TP53 row (Ensembl ID for TP53)
tp53_row <- counts["ENSG00000141510.18", ]

# Transpose so samples become rows, with a column for TP53 expression
tp53_df <- data.frame(
  barcode = colnames(tp53_row),
  TP53_expression = as.numeric(tp53_row[1, ])
)

# Merge with metadata using the shared barcode column
tp53_merged <- merge(tp53_df, meta, by = "barcode")

# Quick check
tp53_merged %>%
  select(barcode, TP53_expression, method_of_diagnosis) %>%
  head(5)

```
b) Generate Summary Statistics: Using the count data from the selected gene, compute
and report summary statistics, such as mean, median, standard deviation, minimum, and
maximum.

```{r}
# Summary of Stats
tp53_summarystats <- tp53_merged %>%
  summarize(
    min = min(TP53_expression, na.rm = TRUE), 
    max = max(TP53_expression, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean = mean(TP53_expression, na.rm = TRUE),
    median = median(TP53_expression, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd = sd(TP53_expression, na.rm = TRUE),
  )
tp53_summarystats #displays summary table
```
3) Visualization:
a) Create a Histogram: Use ggplot2 to generate a histogram of the count data for the
selected gene. This visualization should effectively display the distribution of the counts.

```{r}
library(ggplot2)

p1 <- ggplot(tp53_merged, aes(x = TP53_expression)) + # ggplot2
  geom_histogram(color = "black", binwidth = 500, fill = "#FF1493") + 
    labs(x = "TP53 Count", y = "Number of Samples", title = "Distribution of TP53 Gene Expression") 
# Assigning axis names, title

print(p1) #prints histogram

# Adding log2 transformation for a second histogram

tp53_merged$log2_TP53 <- log2(tp53_merged$TP53_expression + 1)

p2 <- ggplot(tp53_merged, aes(x = log2_TP53)) +
  geom_histogram(color = "black", fill = "#FF1493", binwidth = 0.5) +
  labs(x = "log2(TP53 Count + 1)", y = "Number of Samples",
       title = "Distribution of TP53 Gene Expression (log2 transformed)")

print(p2) #prints histogram

ggsave("/Users/juliannemirmina/Downloads/711_course/Final Project/figures/histogram.png", p2,    width = 6, height = 4, dpi = 300)

p3 <- ggplot(tp53_merged, aes(x = log2_TP53)) +
  geom_density(fill = "#FF1493", alpha = 0.4) +
  labs(x = "TP53 expression (log2)", y = "Density",
       title = "Density of TP53 Gene Expression (log2 transformed)") +
  theme_bw()

# Save png
ggsave("/Users/juliannemirmina/Downloads/711_course/Final Project/figures/densityplot.png", p3,    width = 6, height = 4, dpi = 300)

print(p3)
```

b) Create a Scatter Plot: Select a second gene from the dataset. Create a scatter plot using
ggplot2 to compare the count data of the two selected genes.

```{r}

# Pull out the CHEK2 row from counts
chek2_row <- counts["ENSG00000183765.23", ]

# Reshape into a data frame: one row per sample
chek2_df <- data.frame(
  barcode = colnames(chek2_row),
  CHEK2_expression = as.numeric(chek2_row[1, ])
)

# Merge CHEK2 expression into your existing tp53_merged data frame
tp53_chek2_merged <- merge(tp53_merged, chek2_df, by = "barcode")

# Create Scatter Plot
p1 <- ggplot(tp53_chek2_merged, aes(x = TP53_expression, y = CHEK2_expression)) +
  geom_point(alpha = .9, color = "#FF69B4") +
  labs(x = "TP53 Count", y = "CHEK2 Count", title = "TP53 vs. CHEK2 Expression")

print(p1)

# Add log2 Scatter Plot
p2 <- ggplot(tp53_chek2_merged,
             aes(x = log2(TP53_expression + 1),
                 y = log2(CHEK2_expression + 1))) +
  geom_point(alpha = .9, color = "#FF69B4") +
  labs(x = "log2(TP53 Count + 1)",
       y = "log2(CHEK2 Count + 1)",
       title = "TP53 vs. CHEK2 Expression (log2 transformed)")

print(p2)

# Save png
ggsave("/Users/juliannemirmina/Downloads/711_course/Final Project/figures/scatter.png",   p2, width = 6, height = 4, dpi = 300)


# log2-transformed values so both tests use identical inputs
x <- log2(tp53_chek2_merged$TP53_expression + 1)
y <- log2(tp53_chek2_merged$CHEK2_expression + 1)

# Pearson: tests for a linear relationship using the actual values
# Output: cor (r, -1 to +1), p-value, and 95% confidence interval
cor.test(x, y, method = "pearson")

# Spearman: tests for a monotonic relationship using ranks
# Output: rho (-1 to +1) and p-value (no confidence interval)
cor.test(x, y, method = "spearman", exact = FALSE) 
# exact = FALSE avoids the "cannot compute exact p-value with ties" warning

#Citation: Portions of this code (question 3) were developed with assistance from Claude (Anthropic, 2026), an AI language model, accessed at https://claude.ai. Code was reviewed, tested, and adapted by Julianne Mirmina to meet assignment requirements.

```
c) Create a Violin Plot: Select one covariate from your metadata. Using the count data from the first gene and the selected covariate, generate a violin plot that illustrates the distribution of count data based on the covariate. For example, if you choose “primary_diagnosis”, your plot should display a violin plot for each level in “primary_diagnosis”.

```{r}
# Create Violin Plot
p <- ggplot(tp53_merged, aes(x = method_of_diagnosis, y = TP53_expression, fill = method_of_diagnosis)) +
  geom_violin(trim = FALSE) +
  labs(x = "Method of Diagnosis", y = "TP53 Raw Count",
       title = "Distribution of TP53 Expression by Method of Diagnosis",
       fill = "Method of Diagnosis") +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)) # Avoid overlapping labels
print(p)

# Save png
ggsave("/Users/juliannemirmina/Downloads/711_course/Final Project/figures/violinplot.png",   p,     width = 7, height = 5, dpi = 300)

```

d) Heatmap Analysis:
i) Select 10 genes: Choose a set of 10 different genes from the count matrix for your
heatmap.
ii) Generate a Heatmap: Use the ComplexHeatmap package in R to create a heatmap
of the count data for the selected genes.
iii) Add an Annotation Bar: Include an annotation bar reflecting your chosen covariate
for further context and interpretation of the data.

```{r}
# Load heatmap libraries
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(ComplexHeatmap)
  library(circlize)  # for color mapping
})

# 10 selected genes (Ensembl IDs matching your counts.csv)
selected_genes <- c(
  "ENSG00000141510.18",  # TP53
  "ENSG00000183765.23",  # CHEK2
  "ENSG00000012048.23",  # BRCA1
  "ENSG00000139618.16",  # BRCA2
  "ENSG00000091831.24",  # ESR1
  "ENSG00000082175.15",  # PGR
  "ENSG00000141736.14",  # ERBB2
  "ENSG00000148773.14",  # MKI67
  "ENSG00000146648.19",  # EGFR
  "ENSG00000171862.11"   # PTEN
)

gene_labels <- c("TP53", "CHEK2", "BRCA1", "BRCA2", "ESR1", 
                  "PGR", "ERBB2", "MKI67", "EGFR", "PTEN")

# Subset counts matrix to just these 10 genes (rows = genes, columns = samples)
heatmap_counts <- as.matrix(counts[selected_genes, ])
rownames(heatmap_counts) <- gene_labels

# Match sample order between the matrix and the metadata
meta_ordered <- meta[match(colnames(heatmap_counts), meta$barcode), ]

# Clean up the covariate: literal "NA" strings translate to RStudio 
meta_ordered$method_of_diagnosis[meta_ordered$method_of_diagnosis %in% c("NA", "")] <- NA

# log2 transform for heavily skewed data 
log_counts <- log2(heatmap_counts + 1)


# Heatmap annotations
method_colors <- c(  
  "Core Biopsy"              = "#1B9E77",
  "Surgical Resection"       = "#D95F02",
  "Fine Needle Aspiration"   = "#7570B3",
  "Excisional Biopsy"        = "#E7298A",
  "Cytology"                 = "#66A61E",
  "Biopsy"                   = "#E6AB02",
  "Incisional Biopsy"        = "#A6761D",
  "Ultrasound Guided Biopsy" = "#666666",
  "Unknown"                  = "grey70"
)
column_ha <- HeatmapAnnotation(
  Method_of_Diagnosis = meta_ordered$method_of_diagnosis,
  col = list(
    Method_of_Diagnosis = method_colors),
    na_col = "gray85"
  )

# Create a pink gradient color mapping
log_colors <- colorRamp2(
  c(min(log_counts), mean(range(log_counts)), max(log_counts)),
  c("#FFF0F5", "#FF69B4", "#8B004F")
)

# Create heatmap
ht <- Heatmap(
  log_counts,  
  name = "log2(Counts + 1)",
  col = log_colors,
  top_annotation = column_ha,
  show_row_names = TRUE,
  show_column_names = FALSE,
  cluster_columns = TRUE,
  show_column_dend = FALSE,
  cluster_rows = TRUE,
  column_title = "Samples",
  row_title = "Genes",
  row_names_gp = gpar(fontsize = 8),
  heatmap_legend_param = list(title = "log2(Counts + 1)")
)

draw(ht)

# Save png
png("/Users/juliannemirmina/Downloads/711_course/Final Project/figures/heatmap.png",
    width = 7, height = 5, units = "in", res = 300)
draw(ht)      
dev.off()

```

```{r}

# Summary Stats
method_stats <- tp53_merged %>%
  group_by(method_of_diagnosis) %>% # Split the data into one group per diagnosis method
  summarize(
    n      = n(),
    min    = min(TP53_expression, na.rm = TRUE),
    max    = max(TP53_expression, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean   = mean(TP53_expression, na.rm = TRUE),
    median = median(TP53_expression, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd     = sd(TP53_expression, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
method_stats # Display the summary table

# Summary of Stats Age of Diagnosis  
age_stats <- tp53_merged %>%
  mutate(age_years = as.numeric(age_at_diagnosis) / 365.25) %>%
  summarize(
    n      = sum(!is.na(age_years)),  # Number of samples with a recorded age
    missing = sum(is.na(age_years)), # Number of samples with missing age
    min    = round(min(age_years, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
    max    = round(max(age_years, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
    mean   = round(mean(age_years, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
    median = round(median(age_years, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
    sd     = round(sd(age_years, na.rm = TRUE), 1)
  )
age_stats # Display the summary table
```
